meta.notes: Visit types a person actually goes to. Recommendations in recommendations.json point here through their `journey` steps. Order in this list is the display order. Coverage notes are general guidance for ACA-compliant private plans, not a guarantee for every plan. `kind` is `book` for visits a person books themselves and `follow` for what gets ordered there. `who`, `how`, `say` and `tip` are what the plan shows; [[double brackets]] mark glossary terms (src/lib/terms.js). `time` is a rough length for planning (draft: verify before shipping).

visits.name: Preventive care visit
visits.call: Call your primary care doctor to schedule a visit
visits.say: I’d like to schedule a preventive care visit.
visits.tip: If you bring up a new problem, you may have to pay for that part of the visit.
visits.description: The hub. Most free screenings happen here as questions, quick measurements, or a blood draw. Anything that needs another appointment usually gets ordered here.
visits.coverage: Most plans cover one preventive visit a year at $0.

visits.name: Well-woman visit
visits.call: Call an OB-GYN to schedule a well-woman visit
visits.say: I’d like to schedule a well-woman visit.
visits.description: A yearly preventive visit focused on reproductive and sexual health.
visits.coverage: Covered once a year at $0 under the ACA's women's preventive services.

visits.name: Prenatal visits
visits.how: These are part of your regular pregnancy checkups. There’s nothing extra to schedule.
visits.description: Checkups during pregnancy. Several free screenings and supports are built into this care.
visits.coverage: The preventive screenings listed here are covered at $0.

visits.name: Lab work
visits.who: At the office or a lab
visits.how: Usually one blood draw, often the same day as your visit. Otherwise, take your doctor’s order to a lab.
visits.tip: Plans must cover these tests. Routine panels, like a blood count or vitamin D, aren’t on that list, so you may have to pay for them. Ask before the blood draw.
visits.description: A blood or urine sample. Often taken the same day as your checkup, otherwise at a lab with the order your doctor gives you.
visits.coverage: Covered at $0 when ordered as part of a preventive screening.

visits.name: Imaging appointment
visits.how: Most scans need an order from your doctor. Mammograms often don’t, so you can schedule those yourself.
visits.tip: Free when it’s a screening. If the scan is to look into symptoms, you may have to pay.
visits.description: A scan done somewhere other than your doctor's office, like a mammogram, low-dose CT, ultrasound, or bone density test.
visits.coverage: Covered at $0 when it's a screening, not a follow-up for symptoms.

visits.name: Colon cancer test
visits.how: Your doctor orders it at your visit. You choose which test.
visits.tip: If a home test comes back abnormal, the follow-up colonoscopy should be covered too. Confirm with your plan.
visits.description: You choose the test with your doctor: a stool test you do at home, or a colonoscopy at a GI clinic.

visits.name: Pharmacy pickup
visits.how: Your doctor sends the prescription and you pick it up.
visits.tip: Ask for a generic if there’s a choice. It’s usually the $0 option.
visits.description: Some preventive medicines are free with a prescription from your doctor.
visits.coverage: Covered at $0 with a prescription for eligible people.

visits.name: Coaching program
visits.how: Ongoing sessions with a counselor, dietitian, or coach, not a one-time test.
visits.tip: Check that the program is in-network before you start.
visits.description: Ongoing sessions, not a one-time test. Your doctor refers you.
visits.coverage: Covered at $0 when it meets the preventive guideline.

visits.name: Genetic counseling
visits.how: A conversation about your family history. It usually needs a referral.
visits.description: A conversation about family history and, if it makes sense, genetic testing.
visits.coverage: Counseling, and testing when recommended, is covered at $0 for eligible people.
